ANYbotics launches Shift to connect robot inspections with maintenance

The platform combines fleet missions, contextual analysis and connections to plant maintenance systems.

New Electronics ↗2 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Turning inspection into action

ANYbotics has introduced Shift to connect robot inspection rounds with equipment-maintenance decisions. It brings mission management, data interpretation and business-system handoffs into a common workflow. This is a separate platform launch from the previously covered ANYmal secure-door deployment at Whitegate power station.

Four connected modules

Fleet schedules and monitors missions. Insight evaluates visual, thermal, acoustic and gas readings alongside operating context such as motor load and ambient temperature. Connect sends confirmed anomalies into maintenance systems through connectors and APIs. Maps associates readings with asset identifiers and the plant hierarchy, helping teams locate the equipment requiring attention.

Migration and present scope

ANYbotics says Data Navigator will become Shift through a regular update while retaining existing data and settings. Deployment options include managed regional cloud, a customer’s cloud and on-premise installations where needed. Support for other manufacturers’ robots is a future expansion, rather than evidence of immediate compatibility with every robot brand.
